desc: Ideation: greedy by increasing marginal cost (2j−1)·Pᵢ is optimal (exchange argument); binary search threshold T; kᵢ = (T//Pᵢ + 1)//2; answer = cnt(T) + R//L with L = min next marginal; stock cap 10^100 never binds (kᵢ ≤ √(M/Pᵢ) ≤ 1e9).
Hand-trace algorithm on samples and custom edge cases (extra>0 case, Pᵢ>M case, N=1 P=1 M=10^18 case) — all verified.

Implement solve(): parse stdin; build numpy int64 arrays P and Kcap = isqrt(M//Pᵢ)+1; binary search max T∈[0,M] with capped cost(T) ≤ M (float64 precheck to avoid int64 sum overflow, exact int64 sum when near/below M); final answer = cnt + (M−cost)//L; print.
Verify overflow safety: cap kᵢ before squaring (Kcap = isqrt(M//Pᵢ)+1 keeps kᵢ²Pᵢ ≲ 1.001e18 < 2^63); (2kᵢ+1)Pᵢ ≲ 4e18 < 2^63; float precheck margin 1e8 vs error ~4e3.
Final review of code for correctness and edge cases (N=1, M=1, all Pᵢ > M, T=M boundary).
